items.why: Singling this job out as uniquely suitable, with a negative predicate following, is Point 1's をおいて.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 趣味と実益を兼ねて

items.q: 彼女は自分の失敗（ ）、他人の批判ばかりしている。
items.qr: Kanojo wa jibun no shippai (___), tanin no hihan bakari shite iru.
items.en: Ignoring her own failures, she does nothing but criticize other people.
items.hi: अपनी ही ग़लतियों को नज़रअंदाज़ करते हुए, वह सिर्फ़ दूसरों की आलोचना करती रहती है।
items.gu: પોતાની જ ભૂલોને અવગણીને, તે માત્ર બીજાની ટીકા કરતી રહે છે.
items.why: Disregarding her own faults while criticizing others is Point 2's をよそに.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 趣味と実益を兼ねて

items.q: 観光を（ ）オーストラリアへ研修に行った。
items.qr: Kankou o (___) Oosutoraria e kenshuu ni itta.
items.en: I went to Australia for training, combining it with sightseeing.
items.hi: सैर-सपाटे को भी मिलाकर, ऑस्ट्रेलिया प्रशिक्षण के लिए गया/गई।
items.gu: ફરવાનું પણ ભેગું કરીને, ઓસ્ટ્રેલિયા તાલીમ માટે ગયો/ગઈ.

opts.en: (wrong — sightseeing isn't a required interval that had to elapse first)

items.why: The trip serves two purposes at once (training + sightseeing) — Point 4's かねて, not Point 3's を経て (which needs a prior process/interval).
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 趣味と実益を兼ねて

items.q: 近隣の住民の反対を（ ）、高層マンションが建設されてしまった。
items.qr: Kinrin no juumin no hantai o (___), kousou manshon ga kensetsu sarete shimatta.
items.en: Despite the objections of nearby residents, a high-rise apartment building ended up being constructed.
items.hi: आस-पड़ोस के निवासियों के विरोध की परवाह किए बिना, ऊँची इमारत बना ही दी गई।
items.gu: આસપાસના રહેવાસીઓના વિરોધની પરવા કર્યા વગર, ઊંચી ઇમારત બાંધી જ દેવાઈ.

opts.en: (wrong — opposition isn't a process the building "passed through")

items.why: Residents' opposition being disregarded while construction proceeds anyway is Point 2's をよそに.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 趣味と実益を兼ねて

items.q: 彼女は結婚、出産を（ ）、また競技に復帰した。
items.qr: Kanojo wa kekkon, shussan o (___), mata kyougi ni fukki shita.
items.en: After going through marriage and childbirth, she returned to competition once more.
items.hi: शादी और बच्चे को जन्म देने के बाद, वह फिर से प्रतियोगिता में लौट आई।
items.gu: લગ્ન અને બાળકજન્મ પછી, તે ફરી સ્પર્ધામાં પાછી ફરી.

opts.en: (wrong — marriage and childbirth aren't simultaneous dual purposes, they're a sequence she passed through)

items.why: Marriage and childbirth are life stages she passed through before returning to competition — Point 3's を経て.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 趣味と実益を兼ねて

items.q: その大地震（ ）、各地で地震対策が見直されている。
items.qr: Sono oo-jishin (___), kakuchi de jishin taisaku ga minaosarete iru.
items.en: Taking that major earthquake as the trigger, earthquake preparedness is being reviewed everywhere.
items.hi: उस बड़े भूकंप को अवसर मानकर, हर जगह भूकंप से बचाव के उपायों की समीक्षा हो रही है।
items.gu: તે મોટા ધરતીકંપને તક માનીને, દરેક જગ્યાએ ધરતીકંપ સામેના પગલાંની સમીક્ષા થઈ રહી છે.

opts.en: (wrong — 折に is a polite "at the time of," not a decisive trigger for policy change)

items.why: The earthquake is the deliberate prompt for a nationwide policy review — Point 5's を機に.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 6 · 結婚を前提として

items.q: お近くにお越し（ ）は、是非お立ち寄りください。
items.qr: Ochikaku ni okoshi (___) wa, zehi otachiyori kudasai.
items.en: Please do drop by whenever you're in the area.
items.hi: जब भी आप आस-पास आएँ, तो ज़रूर आकर मिलिए।
items.gu: જ્યારે પણ તમે નજીકમાં આવો, ત્યારે જરૂર મળવા આવો.

opts.en: (wrong — this is a polite invitation, not a stated premise/assumption)

items.why: A polite, gentle invitation phrase ("whenever you happen to be nearby") is Point 4's の折に.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 6 · 結婚を前提として

items.q: 今までの意見を（ ）、この案を採用するかの決定を出したいと思います。
items.qr: Ima made no iken o (___), kono an o saiyou suru ka no kettei o dashitai to omoimasu.
items.en: I would like to make a decision on whether to adopt this proposal, taking the opinions expressed so far into account.
items.hi: अब तक की राय को ध्यान में रखते हुए, इस प्रस्ताव को अपनाया जाए या नहीं, इसका फ़ैसला करना चाहता/चाहती हूँ।
items.gu: અત્યાર સુધીના અભિપ્રાયોને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને, આ દરખાસ્ત સ્વીકારવી કે નહીં, તેનો નિર્ણય લેવા માંગુ છું.

opts.en: (wrong — opinions aren't a turning-point event in time)

items.why: Using prior opinions as the basis for a decision is Point 1's 踏まえて.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 6 · 結婚を前提として

items.q: 結婚を（ ）彼女は会社を退職した。
items.qr: Kekkon o (___) kanojo wa kaisha o taishoku shita.
items.en: Taking her marriage as the occasion, she left her job.
items.hi: शादी को मौक़ा बनाकर, उसने नौकरी छोड़ दी।
items.gu: લગ્નને તક બનાવીને, તેણે નોકરી છોડી દીધી.

opts.en: (wrong — quitting isn't built on marriage as an assumed premise, it's triggered by it)

items.why: Marriage is the trigger event prompting a life decision (quitting work) — Point 5's を機に, not Point 2's を前提として (which states an assumed condition, not a triggering event).
items.unit: Week 6 Day 6 · 結婚を前提として

items.q: 人は40歳を（ ）急に老化が進むそうです。
items.qr: Hito wa yonjussai o (___) kyuu ni rouka ga susumu sou desu.
items.en: They say aging suddenly accelerates for people around the age of 40.
items.hi: कहते हैं कि 40 साल की उम्र के बाद से, बुढ़ापा अचानक तेज़ी से बढ़ने लगता है।
items.gu: કહેવાય છે કે 40 વર્ષની ઉંમર પછીથી, ઘડપણ અચાનક ઝડપથી વધવા લાગે છે.

opts.en: (wrong — 40 isn't evidence being taken into account, it's an age boundary)

items.why: Age 40 is described as a neutral before/after dividing line for aging — Point 3's を境に.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 6 · 結婚を前提として

items.q: 彼のコンサートの模様が10年の月日（ ）ついに映像化された。
items.qr: Kare no konsaato no moyou ga juu-nen no tsukihi (___) tsui ni eizouka sareta.
items.en: After ten years passed, the footage of his concert was finally made into a video.
items.hi: उसके कॉन्सर्ट के दृश्य, 10 साल बीतने के बाद, आख़िरकार वीडियो में ढाले गए।
items.gu: તેના કોન્સર્ટના દ્રશ્યો, 10 વર્ષ વીત્યા પછી, છેવટે વીડિયોમાં બનાવાયા.

opts.en: with... as the dividing line (wrong fit)

items.why: Day 5's を経て — ten years had to elapse before the footage was released.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 容疑者は警官に（ ）パトカーに乗った。
items.qr: Yougisha wa keikan ni (___) patokaa ni notta.
items.en: The suspect got into the patrol car, simply as urged by the police officer.
items.hi: संदिग्ध, पुलिस अफ़सर के कहने पर, बिना विरोध किए गाड़ी में बैठ गया।
items.gu: શંકાસ્પદ, પોલીસ અધિકારીના કહેવા પર, વિરોધ કર્યા વગર ગાડીમાં બેસી ગયો.

opts.en: (wrong tense — needs the plain form まま, not た)
even while being urged (wrong — implies resistance, but he complied)

items.why: Week 6 Day 2's Vる（が）まま — following the officer's direction with no resistance at all.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 父親は、子どもを（ ）、火事で燃えている家に飛び込んでいった。
items.qr: Chichioya wa, kodomo o (___), kaji de moete iru ie ni tobikonde itta.
items.en: The father jumped into the burning house in order to save his child.
items.hi: पिता अपने बच्चे को बचाने के इरादे से, आग में जलते घर में कूद पड़ा।
items.gu: પિતાએ પોતાના બાળકને બચાવવાના ઇરાદાથી, આગમાં સળગતા ઘરમાં કૂદકો માર્યો.

opts.en: ended up never saving (wrong — he did act)

items.why: Day 4's んがために — jumping into a fire is a deliberate, resolved purpose to save the child.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: さあ、最後の練習だ。本番（ ）やってみよう。
items.qr: Saa, saigo no renshuu da. Honban (___) yatte miyou.
items.en: All right, this is the last practice run. Let's try it as if it were the real thing.
items.hi: चलो, आख़िरी अभ्यास है। असली प्रदर्शन समझकर कोशिश करते हैं।
items.gu: ચાલો, છેલ્લી પ્રેક્ટિસ છે. અસલી પ્રદર્શન સમજીને પ્રયત્ન કરીએ.

opts.en: because of (wrong — no cause is stated)
with the mindset of (the real thing)

items.why: Week 6 Day 2's つもりで — adopting the mindset/assumption of the real performance while still practicing.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 生徒たち（ ）、どうしていいかわからないとは言えない。
items.qr: Seito-tachi (___), dou shite ii ka wakaranai to wa ienai.
items.en: Given my position in front of my students, I can't say I don't know what to do.
items.hi: छात्रों के सामने, यह नहीं कह सकता कि मुझे समझ नहीं आ रहा क्या करूँ।
items.gu: વિદ્યાર્થીઓની સામે, એવું ન કહી શકાય કે મને સમજાતું નથી શું કરવું.

opts.en: given my position in front of

items.why: Day 3's の手前 — maintaining face in front of the students who look up to the speaker.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 父は、うるさいと言わん（ ）テレビの電源を切ってしまった。
items.qr: Chichi wa, urusai to iwan (___) terebi no dengen o kitte shimatta.
items.en: My father turned off the TV as if to say "this is too noisy" (without actually saying it).
items.hi: पिताजी ने मानो "शोर बहुत है" कहते हुए, टीवी बंद कर दिया।
items.gu: પિતાજીએ જાણે "બહુ ઘોંઘાટ છે" કહેતાં, ટીવી બંધ કરી દીધું.

opts.en: in order to (wrong — no deliberate goal, this is body language)

items.why: Day 4's とばかりに (here as 言わんばかりに) — silently but clearly conveying "too noisy" through action.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: その事件（ ）、やっと古い法律が改正された。
items.qr: Sono jiken (___), yatto furui houritsu ga kaisei sareta.
items.en: Taking that incident as the trigger, the old law was finally revised.
items.hi: उस घटना को मौक़ा बनाकर, आख़िरकार पुराना क़ानून बदला गया।
items.gu: તે ઘટનાને તક બનાવીને, છેવટે જૂનો કાયદો બદલવામાં આવ્યો.

opts.en: on the occasion of (too weak — no trigger sense)
because of (grammatically odd with 事件 here)

items.why: Day 6's を機に — the incident is the deliberate prompt for finally revising the law.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 今にも（ ）桜のつぼみがふくらんでいる。
items.qr: Ima ni mo (___) sakura no tsubomi ga fukurande iru.
items.en: The cherry blossom buds are swelling, as if about to bloom at any moment.
items.hi: मानो अभी खिलने ही वाली हों, सकुरा की कलियाँ फूल रही हैं।
items.gu: જાણે હમણાં જ ખીલવાની હોય, સાકુરાની કળીઓ ફૂલી રહી છે.

opts.en: with the intention of blooming (wrong — flowers have no intention)

items.why: Day 4's んばかりに — the buds are vividly on the verge of blooming, though not blooming yet.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 私の家は裕福ではないけれど、まさに「（ ）楽しい我が家」です。
items.qr: Watashi no ie wa yuufuku de wa nai keredo, masani "(___) tanoshii wagaya" desu.
items.en: My family isn't wealthy, but it's truly "a poor yet happy home."
items.hi: मेरा घर अमीर तो नहीं है, लेकिन सचमुच "ग़रीब पर ख़ुशहाल घर" है।
items.gu: મારું ઘર શ્રીમંત નથી, પણ ખરેખર "ગરીબ પણ ખુશહાલ ઘર" છે.

opts.en: (wrong — つもり doesn't attach to a factual state like this)
because of being poor (wrong — no purpose/cause reading fits)

items.why: Week 6 Day 3's ながらも — admitting poverty while asserting happiness regardless.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: あなたに出会った日（ ）、私の人生がばら色に変わりました。
items.qr: Anata ni deatta hi (___), watashi no jinsei ga barairo ni kawarimashita.
items.en: Since the day I met you, my life has turned rosy.
items.hi: जिस दिन से तुमसे मिला/मिली, उस दिन से मेरी ज़िंदगी ख़ुशहाल हो गई।
items.gu: જે દિવસથી તને મળ્યો/મળી, તે દિવસથી મારું જીવન સુખી બની ગયું.

opts.en: in contrast to (wrong — no contrast implied)

items.why: Day 6's を境にして — that day marks a clean before/after divide in the speaker's life.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 天気がいいので運動（ ）ハイキングに行きました。
items.qr: Tenki ga ii node undou (___) haikingu ni ikimashita.
items.en: Since the weather was nice, I went hiking, combining it with exercise.
items.hi: मौसम अच्छा था, इसलिए व्यायाम को भी मिलाकर हाइकिंग पर चला/चली गया/गई।
items.gu: હવામાન સારું હતું, એટલે કસરતને પણ ભેગું કરીને હાઇકિંગ પર ગયો/ગઈ.
items.why: Day 5's を兼ねて — the hike serves both exercise and leisure at once.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 貧困（ ）教育が受けられない子どもたちを支援しよう。
items.qr: Hinkon (___) kyouiku ga ukerarenai kodomo-tachi o shien shiyou.
items.en: Let's support children who can't receive an education because of poverty.
items.hi: ग़रीबी की वजह से शिक्षा न पा सकने वाले बच्चों की मदद करें।
items.gu: ગરીબીના કારણે શિક્ષણ ન મેળવી શકતાં બાળકોને મદદ કરીએ.
items.why: Day 4's ゆえに — poverty is stated as the formal cause for missing an education.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 時代（ ）制度の改革が求められている。
items.qr: Jidai (___) seido no kaikaku ga motomerarete iru.
items.en: Reform of the system in keeping with the times is called for.
items.hi: समय के अनुरूप व्यवस्था में सुधार की माँग की जा रही है।
items.gu: સમય અનુસાર વ્યવસ્થામાં સુધારાની માંગ થઈ રહી છે.
items.why: Week 6 Day 1's Nに即した — reform must fit exactly with the current era.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 日々の散歩の折に、（ ）。
items.qr: Hibi no sanpo no ori ni, (___).
items.en: On my daily walks, I enjoy the changing of the seasons.
items.hi: रोज़ की सैर के दौरान, मौसम के बदलाव का आनंद लेता/लेती हूँ।
items.gu: રોજની ફરવાની ટેવ દરમિયાન, ઋતુઓના બદલાવનો આનંદ માણું છું.

opts.t: 季節の移り変わりを楽しんでいます
opts.r: kisetsu no utsurikawari o tanoshinde imasu

opts.t: ついでに郵便局に寄っています
opts.r: tsuide ni yuubinkyoku ni yotte imasu
opts.en: stopping by the post office along the way (plausible, but less natural as the "折に" headline continuation)

opts.t: 隣人との挨拶が苦手です
opts.r: rinjin to no aisatsu ga nigate desu
opts.en: bad at greeting neighbors (a general trait, not tied to the walk itself)

opts.t: 犬にほえられながらも歩いています
opts.r: inu ni hoerare nagara mo aruite imasu
opts.en: walking despite being barked at by dogs (an odd, negative image for a gentle 折に opener)

items.why: Day 6's の折に sets a gentle, polite tone — enjoying the seasons is the most natural, positive continuation of a description of daily walks.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 主人は、私が腹痛で苦しんでいるのをよそに、（ ）。
items.qr: Shujin wa, watashi ga fukutsuu de kurushinde iru no o yoso ni, (___).
items.en: My husband, ignoring the fact that I'm in agony with a stomachache, is fast asleep snoring away.
items.hi: मेरे पति, मेरे पेट दर्द से तड़पने की परवाह किए बिना, ख़र्राटे भरते हुए सो रहे हैं।
items.gu: મારા પતિ, મારા પેટના દુખાવાથી તડપવાની પરવા કર્યા વગર, નસકોરાં બોલાવતાં ઊંઘી રહ્યા છે.

opts.t: 心配そうに私の顔をのぞいている
opts.r: shinpaisou ni watashi no kao o nozoite iru
opts.en: peering at my face with worry (wrong — contradicts をよそに)

opts.t: 病院に連れて行こうと言い出せない
opts.r: byouin ni tsurete ikou to iidasenai
opts.en: can't bring himself to suggest the hospital (shows some concern, weaker fit)

opts.t: 家にある薬を探し回っている
opts.r: ie ni aru kusuri o sagashimawatte iru
opts.en: searching the house for medicine (shows concern, weaker fit)

opts.t: ぐうぐういびきをかいて寝ている
opts.r: guuguu ibiki o kaite nete iru

items.why: Week 6 Day 5's をよそに means total disregard — only sleeping through her pain (option 4) is genuinely indifferent; the others all show some degree of care.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 「プローラ」...ではなく、まずは世界（ ）、3月上旬に、日本での先行発売となります。
items.why: Week 6 Day 1's Nに先駆けて — Japan gets the release before the rest of the world.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: もちろん、世界各国での販売（ ）開発しておりますので…

opts.en: with... as the dividing line (wrong fit)

items.why: Day 6's を前提として — global sales are the underlying assumption the product's development is built on.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: このパソコンは、その軽さ（ ）、機能性にも優れており…

opts.en: (wrong — no concessive contradiction is intended here)

items.why: Day 3's もさることながら — lightness is a given, and functionality is highlighted as equally impressive.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 今まではその軽量（ ）なし得なかった耐久性についても…
items.why: Day 4's ゆえに — being lightweight is stated as the (formal) cause that had previously ruled out good durability.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: この高機能と超軽量の双方を実現できるのは、我が社（ ）と自負しております。

opts.t: を踏まえてほかにない

items.why: Day 5's をおいてほかにない — the company proudly claims no one else could achieve this combination.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 家の中に変なにおいがこもっていたので、窓（ ）窓を全部開けた。
items.qr: Ie no naka ni hen na nioi ga komotte ita node, mado (___) mado o zenbu aketa.
items.en: Since a strange smell had built up in the house, I opened every single window.
items.hi: घर के अंदर अजीब सी बदबू भर गई थी, इसलिए मैंने हर एक खिड़की खोल दी।
items.gu: ઘરની અંદર વિચિત્ર વાસ ભરાઈ ગઈ હતી, એટલે મેં દરેકેદરેક બારી ખોલી નાખી.
items.why: 窓という窓 repeats the same noun (Point 4, NというN) to mean "every single window, no exceptions." 窓に窓 doesn't work because Point 1's N1にN2 needs two different nouns forming a fixed pair (like ごはんにお味噌汁) — it can't be used with the same noun repeated.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 1 · 考えに考えて

items.q: （ ）練習でギターは弾けるようにならないよ。
items.qr: (___) renshuu de gitaa wa hikeru you ni naranai yo.
items.en: You won't become able to play the guitar with just one or two practice sessions.
items.hi: सिर्फ़ एक-दो बार अभ्यास करने से गिटार बजाना नहीं आ पाएगा।
items.gu: ફક્ત એક-બે વાર પ્રેક્ટિસ કરવાથી ગિટાર વગાડતા નહીં આવડે.
items.why: Point 3's N1やN2 needs の before the noun it modifies (like 1万や2万のお金, 3つや4つの子ども in the sidebar box) — 1回や2回の練習 follows that exact shape. も after や2回 breaks the fixed pattern and would shift the nuance toward "even as many as," which isn't what's being said here.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 1 · 考えに考えて

items.q: 彼は（ ）を重ねて、念願の弁護士になった。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) o kasanete, gannen no bengoshi ni natta.
items.en: He piled effort upon effort and became the lawyer he had long dreamed of being.
items.hi: उसने लगातार कड़ी मेहनत करते हुए, आख़िरकार वह वकील बन गया जिसका सपना उसने बरसों से देखा था।
items.gu: તેણે સતત મહેનત પર મહેનત કરીને, છેવટે તે વકીલ બની ગયો જેનું સપનું તેણે વર્ષોથી જોયું હતું.
items.why: This is Point 2's noun-based sibling pattern N に N を重ねて — it needs the bare noun repeated (努力に努力), not a conjugated verb form. Inserting する (努力するに努力) breaks the fixed N+に+N shape. Note the direct callback: this exact phrase 努力に努力を重ねて mirrors this week's own title, 努力に努力を重ねている.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 1 · 考えに考えて

items.q: 娘はおなかがすいていたらしく、（ ）に食べていた。
items.qr: Musume wa onaka ga suite ita rashiku, (___) ni tabete ita.
items.en: My daughter seemed to be hungry, and ate and ate.
items.hi: बेटी को शायद बहुत भूख लगी थी, वह खाती ही चली गई।
items.gu: દીકરીને કદાચ ખૂબ ભૂખ લાગી હતી, તે ખાધે જ રાખતી હતી.
items.why: Point 2's pattern needs the V-ますstem before に (食べに食べて), not the dictionary form. 食べる is the plain/dictionary form and cannot attach directly to に in this construction.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 1 · 考えに考えて

items.q: 私は朝食はいつもコーヒー（ ）パンです。
items.qr: Watashi wa choushoku wa itsumo koohii (___) pan desu.
items.en: For breakfast I always have coffee and bread (as a set).
items.hi: मेरा नाश्ता हमेशा कॉफ़ी के साथ ब्रेड होता है।
items.gu: મારો નાસ્તો હંમેશા કૉફી સાથે બ્રેડ હોય છે.

opts.hi: के साथ (एक तय सेट के रूप में)

items.why: This directly parallels Point 1's opening example (ごはんにお味噌汁) — に marks a fixed, typical combination of two items eaten together. で would only express a generic "with/by means of coffee," which loses the "coffee-and-bread-as-a-set" nuance the sentence needs.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 1 · 考えに考えて

items.q: まだ検討中の（ ）、はっきりとしたお返事はできません。
items.qr: Mada kentouchuu no (___), hakkiri to shita ohenji wa dekimasen.
items.en: Being that it's still under consideration, we can't give you a definite answer yet.
items.hi: अभी विचाराधीन होने के कारण, हम स्पष्ट जवाब नहीं दे सकते।
items.gu: હજુ વિચારણા હેઠળ હોવાના કારણે, અમે સ્પષ્ટ જવાબ આપી શકતા નથી.
items.why: 検討中 (a noun phrase, "under consideration") is being offered as a polite, apologetic reason for the delay — that's exactly N+の+こととて (Point 4). だに (Point 3) marks a minimal trigger for a strong emotional reaction, not a reason clause, so it cannot fit here.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 2 · 思い出すだに

items.q: あんな大きい会社の倒産は、誰もが想像（ ）しなかった。
items.qr: Anna ookii kaisha no tousan wa, dare mo ga souzou (___) shinakatta.
items.en: No one had even imagined that such a large company would go bankrupt.
items.hi: उतनी बड़ी कंपनी के दिवालिया होने की तो किसी ने कल्पना तक नहीं की थी।
items.gu: એટલી મોટી કંપનીના નાદારીની તો કોઈએ કલ્પના પણ કરી નહોતી.
items.why: 想像だにしなかった ("didn't even imagine") is a classic だに (Point 3) construction — the minimal act of imagining didn't even happen. にして (Point 1) marks an exceptional stage/person as a necessary condition, which has no role in this "no one imagined it" sentence.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 2 · 思い出すだに

items.q: これほどの安売りは、現金取引（ ）初めて可能になることだ。
items.qr: Kore hodo no yasuuri wa, genkin torihiki (___) hajimete kanou ni naru koto da.
items.en: A discount this steep is only possible because it's a cash transaction.
items.hi: इतनी बड़ी छूट सिर्फ़ नक़द लेन-देन होने की वजह से ही मुमकिन हो पाती है।
items.gu: આટલું મોટું ડિસ્કાઉન્ટ ફક્ત રોકડ વ્યવહાર હોવાના કારણે જ શક્ય બને છે.
items.why: にして初めて (Point 1) says that only this exceptional condition (a cash transaction) makes the discount possible — exactly the meaning intended. だに (Point 3) has no exceptional-condition sense and doesn't attach naturally to 現金取引 in this way.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 2 · 思い出すだに

items.q: 彼は、授業に遅れてきたのに謝り（ ）席に着いた。
items.qr: Kare wa, jugyou ni okurete kita noni ayamari (___) seki ni tsuita.
items.en: Even though he came late to class, he sat down without even apologizing.
items.hi: वह क्लास में देर से आने के बावजूद, माफ़ी माँगे बिना ही अपनी सीट पर बैठ गया।
items.gu: તે વર્ગમાં મોડો આવવા છતાં, માફી માંગ્યા વગર જ પોતાની બેઠક પર બેસી ગયો.
items.why: もしないで (Point 2) is the exact form the book gives (例：謝りもしないで) — the も adds the critical "didn't even do the minimal courteous thing" nuance fitting his rude behavior. はしないで lacks that も emphasis and isn't the pattern being tested.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 2 · 思い出すだに

items.q: 外国人と結婚するなんて、夢（ ）思わなかった。
items.qr: Gaikokujin to kekkon suru nante, yume (___) omowanakatta.
items.en: I never even dreamed that I would marry a foreigner.
items.hi: किसी विदेशी से शादी करूँगा, यह तो सपने में भी नहीं सोचा था।
items.gu: કોઈ વિદેશી સાથે લગ્ન કરીશ, એવું તો સપનામાં પણ વિચાર્યું નહોતું.
items.why: 夢にだに思わない (Point 3) is a fixed, very common emphatic phrase — "not even in a dream did I think." にして (Point 1) would require 夢 to be treated as an exceptional stage/condition, which is not how "dream" functions in this sentence.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 2 · 思い出すだに

items.q: 彼は中学生になったとたん、大人（ ）ことを言うようになった。
items.qr: Kare wa chuugakusei ni natta totan, otona (___) koto o iu you ni natta.
items.en: The moment he became a junior-high student, he started saying grown-up-sounding things.
items.hi: वह जैसे ही मिडिल स्कूल का छात्र बना, बड़ों जैसी बातें करने लगा।
items.gu: તે જેવો મિડલ સ્કૂલનો વિદ્યાર્થી બન્યો, કે તરત મોટા માણસો જેવી વાતો કરવા લાગ્યો.
items.why: 大人びる is the fixed idiom for a person increasingly looking or sounding grown-up as they mature (Point 2). めく／めいた (Point 1) is reserved for something taking on an abstract impression (mysterious, sarcastic, secretive) — it doesn't naturally combine with 大人 to describe a person's own growth.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 3 · 仕事ぶり

items.q: （ ）薄着などするから風邪をひくんですよ。
items.qr: (___) usugi nado suru kara kaze o hiku ndesu yo.
items.en: You catch a cold because you dress too lightly, acting like you're still young.
items.hi: तुम जवानों जैसा दिखावा करके हल्के कपड़े पहनते हो, इसीलिए सर्दी लग जाती है।
items.gu: તું યુવાન હોવાનો દેખાડો કરીને હલકા કપડાં પહેરે છે, એટલે જ શરદી થઈ જાય છે.
items.why: The speaker criticizes someone for consciously performing youthfulness (dressing light despite their actual age) — that's deliberate pretense, ぶる's territory (Point 3). めく (Point 1) would describe something genuinely becoming youthful, not a willful act of faking it.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 3 · 仕事ぶり

items.q: 親切（ ）近づいてくる人には気をつけてください。
items.qr: Shinsetsu (___) chikazuite kuru hito ni wa ki o tsukete kudasai.
items.en: Please be careful of people who approach you acting falsely kind.
items.hi: कृपया उन लोगों से सावधान रहें जो झूठमूठ दयालु बनने का दिखावा करके पास आते हैं।
items.gu: કૃપા કરીને એવા લોકોથી સાવધ રહો જેઓ ખોટે ખોટા દયાળુ હોવાનો દેખાડો કરીને નજીક આવે છે.

opts.hi: झूठमूठ दयालु बनने का दिखावा करके
opts.gu: ખોટે ખોટા દયાળુ હોવાનો દેખાડો કરીને

items.why: 親切ぶる = deliberately performing kindness to gain trust (Point 3). びる (Point 2) only describes a genuine appearance taken on through growth or age, and 親切びる is not a natural construction at all.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 3 · 仕事ぶり

items.q: 犯行現場には謎（ ）言葉が書かれていた。
items.qr: Hankou genba ni wa nazo (___) kotoba ga kakarete ita.
items.en: A mysterious-sounding message was written at the crime scene.
items.hi: अपराध स्थल पर एक रहस्यमय-सा लगने वाला संदेश लिखा हुआ था।
items.gu: ગુનાના સ્થળે એક રહસ્યમય લાગતો સંદેશો લખેલો હતો.
items.why: 謎めいた is the fixed collocation for something that genuinely carries an air of mystery (Point 1). びた (Point 2) describes a person/thing's appearance from growth or age, which doesn't fit an abstract impression like "mysterious."
items.unit: Week 7 Day 3 · 仕事ぶり

items.q: 選手の活躍（ ）がテレビで紹介されていた。
items.qr: Senshu no katsuyaku (___) ga terebi de shoukai sarete ita.
items.en: The athlete's active performance was featured on TV.
items.hi: टीवी पर खिलाड़ी के शानदार प्रदर्शन के तरीक़े को दिखाया गया था।
items.gu: ટીવી પર ખેલાડીના શાનદાર દેખાવની રીત બતાવવામાં આવી હતી.
items.why: TV news reporting favors the neutral/written ぶり (Point 4); っぷり carries the identical meaning but is the casual, spoken counterpart, which sounds mismatched for a formal news-report register.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 3 · 仕事ぶり

items.q: 電車の中で酔っ払いが聞く（ ）言葉を大声で言っていた。
items.qr: Densha no naka de yopparai ga kiku (___) kotoba o oogoe de itte ita.
items.en: A drunk person on the train was loudly saying things that were unbearable to listen to.
items.hi: ट्रेन में एक शराबी ज़ोर-ज़ोर से ऐसी बातें कह रहा था जो सुनी ही नहीं जा सकती थीं।
items.gu: ટ્રેનમાં એક દારૂડિયો મોટેથી એવી વાતો બોલી રહ્યો હતો જે સાંભળી જ શકાય તેમ નહોતી.
items.why: The drunk person's words are so unpleasant that they cannot be borne — this is Point 2's にたえない (enduring/tolerating something bad). にたりない (Point 4) is about whether something meets a sufficiency standard, which doesn't fit "unbearable words."
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 聞くに堪えない

items.q: 学生生活のいい思い出は、信頼する（ ）教師に出会えたということだ。
items.qr: Gakusei seikatsu no ii omoide wa, shinrai suru (___) kyoushi ni deaeta to iu koto da.
items.en: A great memory of student life is having met a teacher worthy of trust.
items.hi: छात्र जीवन की एक अच्छी याद यह है कि भरोसे के लायक़ शिक्षक से मुलाक़ात हुई।
items.gu: વિદ્યાર્થી જીવનની એક સારી યાદ એ છે કે વિશ્વાસપાત્ર શિક્ષક સાથે મુલાકાત થઈ.
items.why: Point 3's pattern is Vる（またはN）＋に＋足る — the connecting に is mandatory. Option a drops に entirely, which is simply ungrammatical, not a competing grammar point.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 聞くに堪えない

items.q: このシャツは毎日の洗濯（ ）素材で作られています。
items.qr: Kono shatsu wa mainichi no sentaku (___) sozai de tsukurarete imasu.
items.en: This shirt is made of material that can withstand daily washing.
items.hi: यह शर्ट ऐसे कपड़े से बनी है जो रोज़ की धुलाई सहन कर सकता है।
items.gu: આ શર્ટ એવા કાપડમાંથી બનેલું છે જે રોજની ધોલાઈ સહન કરી શકે છે.
items.why: Physically withstanding the wear-and-tear of daily washing is an endurance meaning — Point 1's にたえる. にたる (Point 3) would wrongly frame durable fabric as a "trustworthy/sufficient" judgment rather than a physical-endurance one.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 聞くに堪えない

items.q: 交通事故の現場写真は、見るに（ ）ものばかりだ。
items.qr: Koutsuu jiko no genba shashin wa, miru ni (___) mono bakari da.
items.en: The photos from the accident scene were all things unbearable to look at.
items.hi: सड़क दुर्घटना की मौक़े की तस्वीरें सभी ऐसी थीं जो देखी ही नहीं जा सकती थीं।
items.gu: માર્ગ અકસ્માતના સ્થળના ફોટા બધા જ એવા હતા જે જોઈ શકાય તેમ નહોતા.
items.why: Accident-scene photos are implied to be gruesome, needing the negative 堪えない (Point 2) "unbearable to watch." The positive 堪える (Point 1) would wrongly claim the photos are "worth watching."
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 聞くに堪えない

items.q: この本は子どもたちに推薦する（ ）いい内容だ。
items.qr: Kono hon wa kodomo-tachi ni suisen suru (___) ii naiyou da.
items.en: This book has good content worth recommending to children.
items.hi: इस किताब की सामग्री इतनी अच्छी है कि यह बच्चों को सुझाने लायक़ है।
items.gu: આ પુસ્તકની સામગ્રી એટલી સારી છે કે તે બાળકોને ભલામણ કરવા લાયક છે.
items.why: いい内容 ("good content") signals a positive sufficiency judgment, matching Point 3's に足る. に足りない (Point 4) is the negative and would contradict calling the content いい.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 聞くに堪えない

items.q: 最近の若い女の子は爪を黒や緑に塗っていたりして、見苦しい（ ）。
items.qr: Saikin no wakai onna no ko wa tsume o kuro ya midori ni nutte itari shite, migurushii (___).
items.en: Young girls these days paint their nails black and green and so on — it's indescribably unsightly.
items.hi: आजकल की जवान लड़कियाँ नाखूनों को काले-हरे रंग से रंगती हैं वगैरह, यह देखने में बेहद भद्दा लगता है।
items.gu: આજકાલની યુવાન છોકરીઓ નખને કાળા-લીલા રંગથી રંગે છે વગેરે, જોવામાં અત્યંત બેડોળ લાગે છે.

opts.t: といったらありゃしない
opts.hi: बेहद भद्दा, बयान नहीं कर सकता
opts.gu: અત્યંત બેડોળ, શબ્દોમાં કહી ના શકાય

opts.hi: (यह एक मान्य व्याकरणिक रूप नहीं है)

items.why: 見苦しい (unsightly) is an い-adjective being pushed to an extreme — exactly Point 3's といったらない／ありゃしない job. Option b splices the ったり listing form into Point 4's やしない contraction; that combination isn't a real grammatical pattern and doesn't fit here.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 痛くもなんともない

items.q: 昨日のパーティーでの彼の態度は失礼（ ）なかった。
items.qr: Kinou no paatii de no kare no taido wa shitsurei (___) nakatta.
items.en: His attitude at yesterday's party was incredibly rude, beyond words.
items.hi: कल पार्टी में उसका व्यवहार बेहद बदतमीज़ी भरा था, बयान नहीं कर सकता।
items.gu: ગઈકાલે પાર્ટીમાં તેનું વર્તન અત્યંત અસભ્ય હતું, શબ્દોમાં કહી શકાય નહીં.
items.why: 失礼 is being intensified to an extreme, which is Point 3's job (といったらない). というと means "speaking of X / when it comes to X" — a topic-shift expression with no intensifying force, so it cannot produce the "incredibly rude" meaning needed here.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 痛くもなんともない

items.q: 自分の子がこんな罪を犯すとは、（ ）。
items.qr: Jibun no ko ga konna tsumi o okasu to wa, (___).
items.en: To think that my own child would commit a crime like this — it's indescribably pathetic/pitiful.
items.hi: यह सोचकर ही कि मेरा अपना बच्चा ऐसा अपराध कर सकता है, बेहद दुखद और शर्मनाक लगता है।
items.gu: એ વિચારીને જ કે મારું પોતાનું બાળક આવો ગુનો કરી શકે, અત્યંત દયનીય અને શરમજનક લાગે છે.

opts.t: 情けないといったらない
opts.hi: बेहद दुखद, बयान नहीं कर सकता
opts.gu: અત્યંત દયનીય, શબ્દોમાં કહી ના શકાય

opts.t: 情けなくもなんともない
opts.r: nasakenaku mo nan to mo nai
opts.en: not pathetic at all (wrong — opposite meaning)
opts.hi: बिल्कुल भी दुखद नहीं (ग़लत — विपरीत अर्थ)

items.why: Why — this is the day's classic trap: The context (a parent horrified their own child committed a crime) calls for Point 3's intensifier といったらない — "indescribably pathetic." Option b is Point 2's negator くもなんともない, which would mean "not pathetic at all," the exact opposite of the intended meaning and a direct contradiction of the context. Always check whether the sentence wants a quality amplified (
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 痛くもなんともない

items.q: 何度誘われたって、僕はそんなところに（ ）よ。
items.qr: Nando sasowaretatte, boku wa sonna tokoro ni (___) yo.
items.en: No matter how many times I'm invited, there's no way I'm going to a place like that.
items.hi: चाहे जितनी बार बुलाया जाए, मैं ऐसी जगह बिल्कुल नहीं जाऊँगा।
items.gu: ભલે ગમે તેટલી વાર બોલાવે, હું આવી જગ્યાએ જરાય નહીં જાઉં.

opts.hi: (यह एक मान्य व्याकरणिक रूप नहीं है)

items.why: The sentence needs a strong negation of the action "go," which is Point 4's job (Vます stem + やしない). Option b tries to attach といったらない directly to the bare dictionary form 行く, which isn't how Point 3 works, and it produces no negation meaning at all — the wrong tool for this job.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 痛くもなんともない

items.q: 夏までに10キロ（ ）。
items.qr: Natsu made ni juk-kiro (___).
items.en: I'll lose 10 kilos by summer — just watch, I promise.
items.hi: गर्मियों तक 10 किलो वज़न घटाकर दिखाऊँगा।
items.gu: ઉનાળા સુધીમાં 10 કિલો વજન ઘટાડીને બતાવીશ.

opts.t: やせるといったらありゃしない

items.why: This sentence is a declaration of resolve about a future goal — exactly Point 1's job (Vてみせる). Option b's Point 3 pattern intensifies an existing quality/state to an extreme; "losing weight is indescribable" makes no sense as a statement of intent, so it cannot express the promise the sentence needs.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 痛くもなんともない

items.q: 面接の結果は電話で連絡しますので、こちらに（ ）には及びません。
items.qr: Mensetsu no kekka wa denwa de renraku shimasu node, kochira ni (___) ni wa oyobimasen.
items.en: We'll contact you by phone with the interview results, so there's no need for you to come here.
items.hi: इंटरव्यू के नतीजे हम फ़ोन पर बता देंगे, इसलिए यहाँ आने की ज़रूरत नहीं है।
items.gu: ઇન્ટરવ્યુના પરિણામો અમે ફોન પર જણાવીશું, એટલે અહીં આવવાની જરૂર નથી.
items.why: Point 3's pattern に(は)及ばない attaches to the plain dictionary form of the verb (来る), not the negative — "there's no need to come" is expressed by negating 及ぶ itself (及びません), not the verb before it. 来ない には及ばない would be doubly negative and ungrammatical here.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 彼には及ばない

items.q: この交通事故に関しては歩行者側の不注意と（ ）えない。
items.qr: Kono koutsuu jiko ni kanshite wa hokousha-gawa no fuchuui to (___) enai.
items.en: Regarding this traffic accident, I have to say it was the pedestrian's carelessness that caused it.
items.hi: इस सड़क दुर्घटना के बारे में यह कहना ही पड़ेगा कि यह पैदल यात्री की लापरवाही थी।
items.gu: આ માર્ગ અકસ્માત વિશે એ કહેવું જ પડશે કે તે રાહદારીની બેદરકારીને કારણે થયો.
items.why: Point 2's fixed expression is ざるを得ない, built from the classical negative ざる (not the -ず form used elsewhere, like in 言うに及ばず). 言わずを得ない is not a real construction — the required shape is always V-ない stem + ざるを得ない.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 彼には及ばない

items.q: その映画では、主人公が（ ）敵と戦う姿が印象的だった。
items.qr: Sono eiga de wa, shujinkou ga (___) teki to tatakau sugata ga inshouteki datta.
items.en: In that movie, the sight of the protagonist fighting an unseen/invisible enemy was striking.
items.hi: उस फ़िल्म में, नायक का एक अदृश्य दुश्मन से लड़ते हुए दिखना बहुत प्रभावशाली था।
items.gu: તે ફિલ્મમાં, નાયકનું એક અદ્રશ્ય દુશ્મન સામે લડતું દ્રશ્ય ખૂબ પ્રભાવશાળી હતું.
items.why: This is exactly the day's biggest trap. 見えざる敵 uses Point 1's noun-modifying classical ざる ("an enemy that cannot be seen") — it directly modifies 敵 (a noun). 見ざるをえない is Point 2's completely different fixed expression ("cannot avoid seeing"), which is a full predicate and cannot sit in front of a noun like 敵 the way option a does. Same ざる morpheme, two unrelated jobs — see the callout in §3.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 彼には及ばない

items.q: 京都には（ ）が、この町にもお寺がたくさんあります。
items.qr: Kyouto ni wa (___) ga, kono machi ni mo otera ga takusan arimasu.
items.en: It doesn't compare to Kyoto, but this town also has many temples.
items.hi: क्योतो जितना तो नहीं, लेकिन इस शहर में भी बहुत सारे मंदिर हैं।
items.gu: ક્યોટો જેટલું તો નહીં, પણ આ શહેરમાં પણ ઘણાં મંદિરો છે.
items.why: This is Point 4's comparison pattern (Nには及ばない) — the sentence needs the plain predicate form およばない to end the clause naturally before が. およばず is the -ず form used for the fixed idiom 言うに及ばず (Point 3's bonus phrase) or as a connective, not as the main predicate here.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 彼には及ばない

items.q: 彼の言うことは間違っていないので、納得（ ）を得ないだろう。
items.qr: Kare no iu koto wa machigatte inai node, nattoku (___) o enai darou.
items.en: Since what he's saying isn't wrong, we'll probably have no choice but to accept it.
items.hi: उसकी बात ग़लत नहीं है, इसलिए शायद इसे मानना ही पड़ेगा।
items.gu: તેની વાત ખોટી નથી, એટલે કદાચ તે સ્વીકારવું જ પડશે.
items.why: Pure memorization trap from Point 2 — する's classical negative is the irregular せざる, never しざる. しざる simply does not exist in standard Japanese; every する-compound verb (like 納得する here) takes せざるを得ない.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 彼には及ばない

items.q: 彼女は、夫の暴力に（ ）いたが、ついに家を出て行く決心をした。
items.qr: Kanojo wa, otto no bouryoku ni (___) ita ga, tsui ni ie o dete iku kesshin o shita.
items.en: She endured her husband's violence again and again, but finally decided to leave home.
items.hi: वह पति की हिंसा को बार-बार सहती रही, लेकिन आख़िरकार घर छोड़ने का फ़ैसला किया।

items.en: A burglar broke into a house nearby, and apparently not only cash but even things inside the fridge were stolen.
items.hi: पड़ोस में चोर घुस आया, और सुना है नक़दी तो दूर, फ्रिज के अंदर की चीज़ें तक चुरा ले गया।
items.gu: પડોશમાં ચોર ઘૂસી ગયો, અને સાંભળ્યું છે કે રોકડ તો દૂર, ફ્રિજની અંદરની વસ્તુઓ પણ ચોરી ગયો.

opts.en: (wrong — cash wasn't a topic being shelved, it was itself stolen)

items.why: Point 3's N1はおろかN2まで — cash being stolen is already bad, but even the fridge contents being taken makes the burglary sound worse — the required escalating-negative shape.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 10年前ならいざ知らず

items.q: どんな理由（ ）、入会金の返金は認められません。
items.qr: Donna riyuu (___), nyuukaikin no henkin wa mitomeraremasen.
items.en: Whatever the reason may be, refunds of the enrollment fee are not permitted.
items.hi: कारण चाहे जो भी हो, प्रवेश शुल्क की वापसी की अनुमति नहीं है।
items.gu: કારણ ગમે તે હોય, પ્રવેશ ફીનું રિફંડ માન્ય નથી.

opts.en: (wrong — a questioning form, not "no matter what")

items.why: Point 2's どんな〜であれ — no reason, however plausible, changes the no-refund policy.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 10年前ならいざ知らず

items.q: 状況から判断して、彼が犯人であることは想像に（ ）。
items.qr: Joukyou kara handan shite, kare ga hannin de aru koto wa souzou ni (___).
items.en: Judging from the circumstances, it's not hard to imagine that he is the culprit.
items.hi: हालात से अंदाज़ा लगाते हुए, यह कल्पना करना मुश्किल नहीं कि वही अपराधी है।
items.gu: સંજોગો પરથી અંદાજ લગાવતાં, એ કલ્પના કરવી મુશ્કેલ નથી કે તે જ ગુનેગાર છે.

opts.en: (wrong — this judges whether a reaction is warranted, not whether something is easy to picture)

items.why: Point 2's 想像にかたくない — the circumstantial evidence makes it easy to conclude he's the culprit.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 願ってやまない

items.q: 課長が会社を辞めたとしても、驚くには（ ）。
items.qr: Kachou ga kaisha o yameta to shite mo, odoroku ni wa (___).
items.en: Even if the section chief quit the company, it's nothing to be surprised about.
items.hi: भले ही सेक्शन चीफ़ ने कंपनी छोड़ दी हो, इसमें हैरान होने की कोई बात नहीं है।
items.gu: ભલે સેક્શન ચીફે કંપની છોડી દીધી હોય, તેમાં નવાઈ પામવા જેવું કંઈ નથી.

opts.en: (wrong — this is about ease of imagining, not proportionality of a reaction)

items.why: Point 1's 驚くにはあたらない — quitting isn't unusual enough to merit real surprise.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 願ってやまない

items.q: 彼は裁判で無罪を主張しているが、彼のやったことは殺人で（ ）なんだろう。
items.qr: Kare wa saiban de muzai o shuchou shite iru ga, kare no yatta koto wa satsujin de (___) nan darou.
items.en: He claims innocence in court, but if what he did wasn't murder, then what was it?
items.hi: वह अदालत में ख़ुद को निर्दोष बता रहा है, लेकिन उसने जो किया वह हत्या नहीं तो और क्या है।
items.gu: તે કોર્ટમાં પોતાને નિર્દોષ કહી રહ્યો છે, પણ તેણે જે કર્યું તે હત્યા નહીં તો બીજું શું છે.

opts.en: (wrong — not the fixでなくてなんだろう idiom)

items.why: Point 4's Nでなくてなんだろう — a rhetorical way of insisting his act was definitely murder, despite his plea.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 願ってやまない

items.q: 母が死んで10年以上たつのに、父はまだ母を（ ）やまない。
items.qr: Haha ga shinde juu-nen ijou tatsu noni, chichi wa mada haha o (___) yamanai.
items.en: Even though more than ten years have passed since mother died, father still loves her endlessly.
items.hi: माँ को गुज़रे दस साल से ज़्यादा हो गए, फिर भी पिता आज भी उनसे बेइंतहा प्यार करते हैं।
items.gu: માતાને ગુજર્યાને દસ વર્ષથી વધુ થયાં, છતાં પિતા હજુ પણ તેમને અપાર પ્રેમ કરે છે.

opts.en: (wrong — missing the て-form needed before やまない)

items.why: Point 3's V てやまない — father's love hasn't stopped even a decade later; the て-form is required before やまない.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 願ってやまない

items.q: 両親を亡くした彼女の気持ちは察するに（ ）。
items.qr: Ryoushin o nakushita kanojo no kimochi wa sassuru ni (___).
items.en: It's not hard to imagine the feelings of a woman who has lost both parents.
items.hi: जिस महिला ने अपने माता-पिता दोनों को खो दिया, उसकी भावनाओं का अंदाज़ा लगाना मुश्किल नहीं है।
items.gu: જે મહિલાએ પોતાના માતા-પિતા બંનેને ગુમાવ્યાં, તેની લાગણીઓનો અંદાજ લગાવવો મુશ્કેલ નથી.

opts.en: (wrong — this is about ease of inference, not proportionality of a reaction)

items.why: Point 2's 察するにかたくない — easy to infer her grief without being told directly.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 願ってやまない

items.q: 勝ち負けは気にしないと言っても、やはり（ ）越したことはない。
items.qr: Kachimake wa ki ni shinai to itte mo, yahari (___) koshita koto wa nai.
items.en: Even though I say I don't care about winning or losing, winning is still better.
items.hi: भले ही मैं कहूँ कि हार-जीत की परवाह नहीं करता/करती, फिर भी जीतना ही बेहतर है।
items.gu: ભલે હું કહું કે હાર-જીતની પરવા નથી કરતો/કરતી, છતાં જીતવું જ સારું છે.

opts.en: (wrong — に越したことはない needs the plain/dictionary form directly before it, not a conditional ば-form here)

items.why: Point 2's V るに越したことはない — winning is simply the best outcome, stated with the plain dictionary form 勝つ.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 早ければ早いに越したことはない

items.q: 欲を言えば（ ）ないから、このマンションに決めよう。
items.qr: Yoku o ieba (___) nai kara, kono manshon ni kimeyou.
items.en: If we start being picky there's no end to it, so let's just decide on this apartment.
items.hi: ज़्यादा माँगें रखने लगें तो कोई अंत नहीं है, इसलिए इसी फ़्लैट पर तय कर लेते हैं।
items.gu: વધારે માંગણીઓ કરવા લાગીએ તો કોઈ અંત નથી, એટલે આ જ ફ્લેટ પર નક્કી કરીએ.

opts.en: (wrong particle — the fixed idiom takes が, not も)

items.why: Point 4's V ばきりがない — being greedy about a home purchase could go on forever, so it's better to just decide.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 早ければ早いに越したことはない

items.q: 性能が同じなら、価格が（ ）越したことはない。
items.qr: Seinou ga onaji nara, kakaku ga (___) koshita koto wa nai.
items.en: If the performance is the same, a lower price is naturally better.
items.hi: अगर परफ़ॉर्मेंस एक जैसी है, तो क़ीमत कम होना ही बेहतर है।
items.gu: જો કામગીરી સરખી હોય, તો કિંમત ઓછી હોવી જ સારી.

opts.en: (wrong — に越したことはない needs に, not と)

items.why: Point 2's Aいに越したことはない — a lower price is the obviously preferable choice when quality is equal.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 早ければ早いに越したことはない

items.q: この場所なら、喫煙しても（ ）。
items.qr: Kono basho nara, kitsuen shite mo (___).
items.en: In this spot, it's fine to smoke.
items.hi: इस जगह पर सिगरेट पीने में कोई हर्ज़ नहीं है।
items.gu: આ જગ્યાએ ધૂમ્રપાન કરવામાં કોઈ વાંધો નથી.

opts.en: (less natural — 差し支え is treated as a noun paired with ある/ない, so the standard polite negative is 差し支えありません)

items.why: Point 1's 差し支えない — its polite form pairs 差し支え(noun) with ありません, matching the pattern shown in the book's own connection box (差し支えない, not a directly-conjugated 差し支えます／差し支えません).
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 早ければ早いに越したことはない

items.q: 不満を言うと（ ）けれど、今の会社を辞めるわけにはいかない。
items.qr: Fuman o iu to (___) keredo, ima no kaisha o yameru wake ni wa ikanai.
items.en: If I start listing complaints there's no end to it, but I can't just quit my current job.
items.hi: शिकायतें गिनाने बैठूँ तो कोई अंत नहीं, लेकिन मौजूदा नौकरी छोड़ भी नहीं सकता/सकती।
items.gu: ફરિયાદો ગણાવવા બેસું તો કોઈ અંત નથી, પણ હાલની નોકરી છોડી પણ ન શકાય.
items.why: Point 4's V るときりがない — once complaints start, they could go on endlessly, but quitting isn't a realistic option.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 早ければ早いに越したことはない

items.q: 政治家の汚職を見るにつけ怒りを（ ）。
items.qr: Seijika no oshoku o miru ni tsuke ikari o (___).
items.en: Every time I see politicians' corruption, I can't help but feel angry.
items.hi: नेताओं का भ्रष्टाचार देखकर हर बार ग़ुस्सा आए बिना नहीं रहता।
items.gu: નેતાઓનો ભ્રષ્ટાચાર જોઈને દર વખતે ગુસ્સો આવ્યા વગર રહેતો નથી.

opts.en: (wrong — this is about an externally forced action, not an uncontrollable feeling)

items.why: Point 1's Nを禁じ得ない — witnessing corruption repeatedly triggers uncontrollable anger.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 延期を余儀なくされた

items.q: 昨日の彼らのコンサートでは、興奮のあまり気を失う少女が出る（ ）。
items.qr: Kinou no karera no konsaato de wa, koufun no amari ki o ushinau shoujo ga deru (___).
items.en: At their concert yesterday, things got to the point where girls fainted from excitement.
items.hi: कल उनके कॉन्सर्ट में, उत्साह में इतनी लड़कियाँ बेहोश तक हो गईं।
items.gu: ગઈકાલે તેમના કોન્સર્ટમાં, ઉત્સાહમાં એટલી છોકરીઓ બેભાન પણ થઈ ગઈ.

opts.en: (wrong — this is a habitual/recurring tendency, not a one-time extreme outcome)
things got to the point that

items.why: Point 4's V る始末だ — fainting was the extreme final outcome of the crowd's excitement, a one-off bad result, not a recurring tendency.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 延期を余儀なくされた

items.q: 彼女は大げさに言う（ ）から、そのつもりで聞くように。
items.qr: Kanojo wa oogesa ni iu (___) kara, sono tsumori de kiku you ni.
items.en: She tends to exaggerate, so listen to her with that in mind.
items.hi: वह बात बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर कहने की आदी है, इसलिए यह ध्यान में रखकर सुनना।
items.gu: તે વાત વધારીને કહેવાનું વલણ ધરાવે છે, એટલે એ ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને સાંભળજો.

opts.en: (wrong — this describes a recurring habit, not a single bad final outcome)

items.why: Point 3's V る嫌いがある — describes her ongoing, habitual tendency to exaggerate.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 延期を余儀なくされた

items.q: すぐ治るけがだと言われたのに無理をしたため、手術（ ）。
items.qr: Sugu naoru kega da to iwareta noni muri o shita tame, shujutsu (___).
items.en: Even though I was told it was an injury that would heal quickly, because I pushed myself too hard, I was forced to have surgery.
items.hi: कहा तो गया था कि चोट जल्दी ठीक हो जाएगी, लेकिन ज़्यादा ज़ोर लगाने की वजह से सर्जरी करानी ही पड़ी।
items.gu: કહેવાયું હતું કે ઈજા જલ્દી સારી થઈ જશે, પણ વધારે પડતું જોર કરવાના કારણે સર્જરી કરાવવી જ પડી.

opts.en: (wrong — surgery is an externally forced action, not the speaker's own suppressed emotion)

items.why: Point 2's Nを余儀なくされる — overexertion left no choice but surgery, an outcome forced by circumstances.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 延期を余儀なくされた

items.q: うちの娘は、ダイエットのしすぎで病気になり、（ ）始末だ。
items.qr: Uchi no musume wa, daietto no shisugi de byouki ni nari, (___) shimatsu da.
items.en: My daughter dieted so much that she got sick, and it ended up with her being hospitalized.
items.hi: मेरी बेटी डाइटिंग ज़्यादा करने से बीमार पड़ गई, और आख़िर में अस्पताल में भर्ती होना पड़ा।
items.gu: મારી દીકરી ડાયટિંગ વધારે પડતું કરવાથી બીમાર પડી ગઈ, અને છેવટે હોસ્પિટલમાં દાખલ થવું પડ્યું.

opts.en: (wrong tense — 始末だ attaches to the plain dictionary form, not the past tense)

items.why: Point 4's V る始末だ — the dictionary form 入院する is required directly before 始末だ, regardless of when the event happened.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 延期を余儀なくされた

items.q: 私は貧乏（ ）環境で育ったので、外食などしたことがなかった。
items.qr: Watashi wa binbou (___) kankyou de sodatta node, gaishoku nado shita koto ga nakatta.
items.en: I grew up in an extremely poor environment, so I'd never eaten out at a restaurant.
items.hi: मैं बेहद ग़रीब माहौल में पला-बढ़ा/पली-बढ़ी, इसलिए बाहर खाना खाने जैसा कुछ कभी नहीं किया।
items.gu: હું અત્યંત ગરીબ વાતાવરણમાં ઉછર્યો/ઉછરી, એટલે બહાર જમવા જવા જેવું ક્યારેય કર્યું નહોતું.

opts.en: (wrong — 貧乏 is behaving as a na-adjective here, describing 環境 directly, not a bare noun taking の極み)

items.why: Point 2's な-adj + 極まりない — 貧乏 functions as a na-adjective modifying 環境, matching the 極まりない pattern, not の極み's noun pattern.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · 光栄の至り

items.q: 戦争が長く続くその地域の人々の生活は、悲惨（ ）。
items.qr: Sensou ga nagaku tsuzuku sono chiiki no hitobito no seikatsu wa, hisan (___).
items.en: The lives of the people in that region, where war has dragged on, are extremely tragic.
items.hi: उस क्षेत्र के लोगों की ज़िंदगी, जहाँ युद्ध लंबे समय से चल रहा है, बेहद दुखद है।
items.gu: તે વિસ્તારના લોકોનું જીવન, જ્યાં યુદ્ધ લાંબા સમયથી ચાલી રહ્યું છે, અત્યંત દુઃખદ છે.

opts.en: (wrong — 悲惨 is a な-adjective here, so it needs 極まりない, not の極み)

items.why: Point 2's な-adj + 極まりない — 悲惨 (tragic) is a na-adjective, so it takes 極まりない, not の極み which requires a bare noun before it.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · 光栄の至り

items.q: その映画の残酷（ ）シーンはカットされた。
items.qr: Sono eiga no zankoku (___) shiin wa katto sareta.
items.en: The extremely cruel scenes of that movie were cut.
items.hi: उस फ़िल्म के बेहद क्रूर दृश्य काट दिए गए।
items.gu: તે ફિલ્મના અત્યંત ક્રૂર દ્રશ્યો કાપી નાખવામાં આવ્યા.

opts.en: (wrong — の至り is reserved for a narrow set of feeling-nouns, not for intensifying an adjective like 残酷 before a noun it modifies)

items.why: Point 1's な-adj + 極まる directly modifying a following noun — 残酷極まるシーン ("scenes that are cruel in the extreme").
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · 光栄の至り

items.q: あなたのような大スターとお会いできるなんて感激の（ ）です。
items.qr: Anata no you na daisutaa to oai dekiru nante kangeki no (___) desu.
items.en: Being able to meet a huge star like you is the height of thrilling honor.
items.hi: आप जैसे बड़े स्टार से मिल पाना, यह बड़े सौभाग्य और रोमांच की बात है।
items.gu: તમારા જેવા મોટા સ્ટારને મળી શકવું, આ ખૂબ મોટા સૌભાગ્ય અને રોમાંચની વાત છે.

opts.en: (wrong — the idiom is 極まりない/極まる, not a bare 極まり form)

items.why: Point 4's 感激の至り — the book explicitly marks this pairing valid (○感激の至り), alongside 感激の極み from Point 3.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · 光栄の至り

items.q: あなたにとっては日常的なことかもしれませんが、私にとってはそれは贅沢（ ）です。
items.qr: Anata ni totte wa nichijouteki na koto kamo shiremasen ga, watashi ni totte wa sore wa zeitaku (___) desu.
items.en: This might be an everyday thing for you, but for me it's the height of luxury.
items.hi: आपके लिए यह रोज़मर्रा की बात हो सकती है, लेकिन मेरे लिए यह ऐशो-आराम की पराकाष्ठा है।
items.gu: તમારા માટે આ રોજિંદી વાત હોઈ શકે, પણ મારા માટે આ મોજશોખની પરાકાષ્ઠા છે.

opts.en: (wrong — not a real form; it's either 極まる/極まりない or の極み, never の極まり)

items.why: Point 3's N の極み — 贅沢の極み is one of the book's own listed set phrases ("the height of luxury").
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · 光栄の至り

items.q: 昨日見た報道番組では、この世に（ ）光景が次々と流された。
items.qr: Kinou mita houdou bangumi de wa, kono yo ni (___) koukei ga tsugitsugi to nagasareta.
items.en: In the news program I watched yesterday, scene after scene that should never exist in this world was broadcast.
items.hi: कल जो न्यूज़ प्रोग्राम देखा उसमें, ऐसे दृश्य दिखाए गए जो इस दुनिया में होने ही नहीं चाहिए थे।
items.gu: ગઈકાલે જોયેલા ન્યૂઝ પ્રોગ્રામમાં, એવા દ્રશ્યો બતાવાયા જે આ દુનિયામાં હોવા જ ન જોઈએ.

opts.en: (wrong — a bare predicate, cannot directly modify the following noun 光景)

items.why: Point 5's N にあるまじきN — あるまじき is the attributive form needed to directly modify the following noun 光景 ("scenes").
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · 子どもじゃあるまいし

items.q: 野菜が体にいいのはわかるが、（ ）こんなにたくさんは食べられない。
items.qr: Yasai ga karada ni ii no wa wakaru ga, (___) konna ni takusan wa taberarenai.
items.en: I know vegetables are good for you, but I'm not a horse — I can't eat this much.
items.hi: सब्ज़ियाँ सेहत के लिए अच्छी हैं, यह पता है, लेकिन मैं घोड़ा तो नहीं हूँ कि इतनी सारी खा सकूँ।
items.gu: શાકભાજી સ્વાસ્થ્ય માટે સારા છે, એ ખબર છે, પણ હું ઘોડો તો નથી કે આટલું બધું ખાઈ શકું.

opts.en: it's not like I'm a horse
(wrong particle — the idiom takes では／じゃ, not には)

items.why: Point 4's N じゃあるまいし — since the speaker obviously isn't a horse, eating that much is unreasonable.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · 子どもじゃあるまいし

items.q: 彼女は足の痛み（ ）マラソンを走り抜いた。
items.qr: Kanojo wa ashi no itami (___) marason o hashirinuita.
items.en: She ran through the marathon, undeterred by the pain in her leg.
items.hi: उसने पैर के दर्द की परवाह किए बिना मैराथन पूरी की।
items.gu: તેણે પગના દુખાવાની પરવા કર્યા વગર મેરેથોન પૂરી કરી.

opts.en: (wrong — this needs a role noun + a following noun like 行為, not an obstacle being overcome)

opts.r: o mono to mo sezu ni

items.why: Point 3's N をものともせずに — she pushed through the marathon despite the pain, treating it as no obstacle at all.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · 子どもじゃあるまいし

items.q: 弱い者をだまして金を取るなど、人間に（ ）行為だ。
items.qr: Yowai mono o damashite kane o toru nado, ningen ni (___) koui da.
items.en: Deceiving the weak to take their money is conduct unbecoming of a human being.
items.hi: कमज़ोरों को धोखा देकर पैसे लेना, यह इंसान के तौर पर बिल्कुल अनुचित काम है।
items.gu: નબળાઓને છેતરીને પૈસા લેવા, આ માણસ તરીકે તદ્દન અયોગ્ય કૃત્ય છે.

opts.en: (wrong — this dismisses a possibility as a lead-in, it doesn't modify a following noun like 行為)

items.why: Point 5's N にあるまじき行為 — deceiving vulnerable people is fundamentally incompatible with being human.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · 子どもじゃあるまいし

items.q: 人は、（ ）悩みはあるものです。
items.qr: Hito wa, (___) nayami wa aru mono desu.
items.en: People, to a greater or lesser degree, have worries.
items.hi: इंसान को कम या ज़्यादा, कोई न कोई चिंता ज़रूर होती है।
items.gu: માણસને ઓછી કે વધારે, કોઈને કોઈ ચિંતા ચોક્કસ હોય છે.

opts.t: 多くにつけ少なくにつけ
opts.r: ooku ni tsuke sukunaku ni tsuke
opts.en: (wrong — not a real fixed idiom; につけ pairs with 良い/悪い-type opposites, not 多い/少ない)

items.why: Point 1's 多かれ少なかれ — one of the fixed かれ-paired idioms, "to some degree, whether more or less."
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · 子どもじゃあるまいし

items.q: 一見平和に見えるこの国だが、（ ）ほどの問題を抱えている。
items.qr: Ikken heiwa ni mieru kono kuni da ga, (___) hodo no mondai o kakaete iru.
items.en: This country may look peaceful at first glance, but it has more problems than can be counted.
items.hi: यह देश देखने में शांत लगता है, लेकिन इसकी समस्याएँ गिनी न जा सकें इतनी हैं।
items.gu: આ દેશ જોવામાં શાંત લાગે છે, પણ તેની સમસ્યાઓ ગણી ન શકાય એટલી છે.

opts.t: 数えるにこしたことがない
opts.r: kazoeru ni koshita koto ga nai
opts.en: (wrong — に越したことはない means "best to," not "endless")
too many to count, no end to them

opts.t: 数えるにはあたらない

opts.en: (wrong — "not hard to count," opposite of the intended meaning)

items.why: Day 3's V ばきりがない — the country's problems have no natural stopping point if you tried to count them.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 小学生（ ）、大学生にもなってこんな簡単な算数がわからないとは情けない。
items.qr: Shougakusei (___), daigakusei ni mo natte konna kantan na sansuu ga wakaranai to wa nasakenai.
items.en: I don't know about elementary schoolers, but for a university student not to understand such simple arithmetic is pathetic.
items.hi: प्राइमरी के बच्चों की तो बात छोड़ो, यूनिवर्सिटी में पढ़कर भी इतना आसान गणित न समझना शर्मनाक है।
items.gu: પ્રાઇમરીના બાળકોની તો વાત છોડો, યુનિવર્સિટીમાં ભણીને પણ આટલું સહેલું ગણિત ન સમજવું શરમજનક છે.

opts.en: I don't know about (elementary schoolers), but
(wrong — needs a second, more extreme noun escalation, not a contrast with the present)

opts.r: o mono to mo sezu ni

items.why: Day 1's N ならいざ知らず — elementary schoolers are set aside as a separate, forgivable case before judging university students harshly.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 私の隣に座っていた人は、コンサートの開始に遅れただけではなく、居眠り（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi no tonari ni suwatte ita hito wa, konsaato no kaishi ni okureta dake de wa naku, inemuri (___).
items.en: The person sitting next to me wasn't only late for the concert's start — it got to the point where they even dozed off.
items.hi: मेरे बगल में बैठा व्यक्ति न सिर्फ़ कॉन्सर्ट की शुरुआत में देर से आया, बल्कि झपकी तक ले बैठा।
items.gu: મારી બાજુમાં બેઠેલી વ્યક્તિ ફક્ત કોન્સર્ટની શરૂઆતમાં મોડી નહોતી આવી, પણ ઝોકું પણ ખાઈ બેઠી.

opts.en: (wrong — の至り pairs with a narrow set of feeling-nouns, not a described bad habit)
(wrong — this is the speaker's own suppressed emotion, not someone else's dozing off)
it got to the point of even (dozing off)
(wrong — dozing off isn't an externally forced necessity)

items.why: Day 4's V る始末だ — being late escalates to the worse, final low point of falling asleep.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 「酔っていたとはいえ、失礼（ ）態度を取ってしまい、誠に申し訳ありませんでした。」
items.qr: "Yotte ita to wa ie, shitsurei (___) taido o totte shimai, makoto ni moushiwake arimasen deshita."
items.en: "Even though I was drunk, I ended up behaving extremely rudely, and I am truly sorry."
items.hi: "भले ही मैं नशे में था/थी, लेकिन बेहद बदतमीज़ी से पेश आया/आई, इसके लिए सच में माफ़ी चाहता/चाहती हूँ।"
items.gu: "ભલે હું નશામાં હતો/હતી, પણ અત્યંત અસભ્યતાથી વર્ત્યો/વર્તી, તે માટે ખરેખર માફી માંગું છું."

opts.en: (wrong — needs a role noun + にあるまじき, no role is named here)
(wrong — の至り doesn't modify an adjective like 失礼 this way)

items.why: Day 5's な-adj + 極まりない — 失礼 is a na-adjective, intensified to its extreme.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 仲間が海で遭難した。彼らの無事を（ ）。
items.qr: Nakama ga umi de sounan shita. Karera no buji o (___).
items.en: My companions were shipwrecked at sea. I sincerely and constantly pray for their safety.
items.hi: मेरे साथी समुद्र में फँस गए। मैं लगातार उनकी सलामती की दुआ करता/करती हूँ।
items.gu: મારા સાથીઓ સમુદ્રમાં ફસાયા. હું સતત તેમની સલામતી માટે પ્રાર્થના કરું છું.

opts.en: (wrong — 始末だ marks a bad final outcome, not a sincere ongoing wish)
(wrong — not hard to wish is not the intended meaning)

items.why: Day 2's V てやまない — an intense, unceasing hope for the missing companions' safety.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 首相が辞任したのは、筋書き通りで（ ）。
items.qr: Shushou ga jinin shita no wa, sujigaki doori de (___).
items.en: The prime minister's resignation went exactly according to the script, so it was nothing to be surprised about.
items.hi: प्रधानमंत्री का इस्तीफ़ा बिल्कुल तय पटकथा के अनुसार हुआ, इसलिए हैरान होने की कोई बात नहीं थी।
items.gu: વડાપ્રધાનનું રાજીનામું બિલકુલ નક્કી પટકથા મુજબ થયું, એટલે નવાઈ પામવા જેવું કંઈ નહોતું.

opts.t: 驚くことにこしたことはなかった
opts.r: odoroku koto ni koshita koto wa nakatta

opts.t: 驚きにかたくなかった
opts.en: (wrong — に難くない pairs with imagining/inferring, not with 驚き itself as a bare reaction)

opts.t: 驚きを禁じ得なかった
opts.en: (wrong sense — this would mean the surprise WAS overwhelming, opposite of "expected")

opts.t: 驚くにはあたらなかった
opts.en: was nothing to be surprised about

items.why: Day 2's V るにはあたらない — since it went exactly as scripted, surprise would be disproportionate.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: A社は昨今の不景気（ ）、業績を伸ばしている。
items.qr: Eishisha wa sakkon no fukeiki (___), gyouseki o nobashite iru.
items.en: Company A, undeterred by the recent recession, is growing its business results.
items.hi: कंपनी A, हाल की मंदी की परवाह किए बिना, अपना कारोबार बढ़ा रही है।
items.gu: કંપની A, તાજેતરની મંદીની પરવા કર્યા વગર, પોતાનો કારોબાર વધારી રહી છે.

opts.en: (wrong — needs a second, more extreme noun, not a single obstacle being defied)
(wrong particle/pattern — いざ知らず takes なら／は, not を)
(wrong — this shelves a topic, it doesn't describe overcoming an obstacle)

items.why: Day 6's N をものともせずに — the recession doesn't stop the company's growth.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 馬（ ）、こんなにたくさんのニンジンは食べられませんよ。
items.qr: Uma (___), konna ni takusan no ninjin wa taberaremasen yo.
items.en: I'm not a horse — I can't eat this many carrots!
items.hi: मैं घोड़ा तो नहीं हूँ, इतनी सारी गाजरें नहीं खा सकता/सकती!
items.gu: હું ઘોડો તો નથી, આટલી બધી ગાજર ખાઈ ન શકું!

opts.en: (wrong sense — no "no matter what" meaning fits here)
(wrong — no escalating comparison between two nouns here)
(wrong — にあるまじき needs a role + a following noun like 行為, not this shape)

items.why: Day 6's N じゃあるまいし — dismisses being a horse as obviously false, before the complaint about quantity.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 特に秘密にしているわけではないので、（ ）。
items.qr: Toku ni himitsu ni shite iru wake de wa nai node, (___).
items.en: It's not something I'm keeping especially secret, so there's no problem telling anyone.
items.hi: यह ख़ास तौर पर छिपाई गई बात नहीं है, इसलिए किसी को भी बताने में कोई हर्ज़ नहीं है।
items.gu: આ ખાસ છુપાવેલી વાત નથી, એટલે કોઈને પણ કહેવામાં કોઈ વાંધો નથી.

opts.t: 誰に話しても極まりません
誰かに話すにはあたりません
opts.r: dareka ni hanasu ni wa atarimasen
opts.en: (wrong sense — にはあたらない judges a disproportionate reaction, not permission to speak)

opts.t: 誰かに話すにこしたことはありません
opts.r: dareka ni hanasu ni koshita koto wa arimasen
opts.en: (wrong sense — this claims telling someone is "best," not merely "fine")

opts.t: 誰に話しても差し支えありません
opts.r: dare ni hanashite mo sashitsukae arimasen
opts.en: no problem at all telling anyone

items.why: Day 3's 〜ても差し支えない — since it isn't a secret, telling anyone poses no obstacle.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 経営の危機に面して、社長はリストラの決断をしたが、彼の決断はいつも（ ）。
items.qr: Keiei no kiki ni menshite, shachou wa risutora no ketsudan o shita ga, kare no ketsudan wa itsumo (___).
items.en: Facing a management crisis, the president decided on restructuring, but his decisions always tend to come too late.
items.hi: प्रबंधन संकट का सामना करते हुए, अध्यक्ष ने पुनर्गठन का फ़ैसला किया, लेकिन उनके फ़ैसले हमेशा देर से आने की प्रवृत्ति रखते हैं।
items.gu: સંચાલન કટોકટીનો સામનો કરતાં, પ્રમુખે પુનર્ગઠનનો નિર્ણય લીધો, પણ તેમના નિર્ણયો હંમેશા મોડા આવવાનું વલણ ધરાવે છે.

opts.t: 遅すぎるきらいがある

opts.en: (wrong form — 極まりない attaches to na-adjective stems, not く-adverb forms)

opts.t: 遅いにこしたことはない
opts.r: osoi ni koshita koto wa nai
opts.en: (wrong sense — this would mean "being late is best," the opposite of the criticism intended)

opts.t: 遅くても差し支えない
opts.en: (wrong sense — "it's fine to be late" contradicts the critical tone)

items.why: Day 4's V るすぎる嫌いがある — a recurring, criticized tendency for the president's decisions to be late.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 偽造した硬貨を自動販売機などで使用する事件が相次いだため、その硬貨のデザインや材質の（ ）。
items.qr: Gizou shita kouka o jidou hanbaiki nado de shiyou suru jiken ga aitsuida tame, sono kouka no dezain ya zairyou no (___).
items.en: Because incidents of using counterfeit coins in vending machines and the like occurred one after another, the coin's design and material had to be changed.
items.hi: नक़ली सिक्कों को वेंडिंग मशीनों में इस्तेमाल करने की घटनाएँ लगातार होने की वजह से, उस सिक्के के डिज़ाइन और सामग्री में बदलाव करना ही पड़ा।
items.gu: નકલી સિક્કાઓને વેન્ડિંગ મશીનોમાં વાપરવાની ઘટનાઓ સતત બનવાના કારણે, તે સિક્કાની ડિઝાઇન અને સામગ્રીમાં ફેરફાર કરવો જ પડ્યો.

opts.t: 変更を禁じえなかった
opts.en: (wrong — this is an uncontrollable feeling, not an official forced action)
(not a valid/natural combination in this sense)

opts.t: 変更を余儀なくされた
変更をものともしなかった
opts.r: henkou o mono to mo shinakatta
opts.en: (wrong sense — this would mean the change was defied/ignored, not that it happened)

items.why: Day 4's N を余儀なくされる — repeated counterfeiting incidents left no choice but to change the coin's design.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 若いときならいざ知らず、（ ）。
items.qr: Wakai toki nara iza shirazu, (___).
items.en: I don't know about when I was young, but I can't do such intense exercise now.
items.hi: जवानी के दिनों की तो बात छोड़िए, अब ऐसी कठोर कसरत नहीं हो पाती।
items.gu: યુવાનીના દિવસોની તો વાત છોડો, હવે એવી સખત કસરત નથી થઈ શકતી.

opts.t: 年を取るのは避けられません
opts.r: toshi o toru no wa sakeraremasen
opts.en: (too generic — doesn't follow from the "back then vs. now" contrast set up)

opts.t: 年を取りたくないものです
opts.en: (off-topic — expresses a wish, not a concrete present-day contrast)

opts.t: 今はそんなきつい運動はできません
opts.r: ima wa sonna kitsui undou wa dekimasen
opts.en: now I can't do such intense exercise

opts.t: 今は運動がきつくても少しずつやっています
opts.r: ima wa undou ga kitsukute mo sukoshizutsu yatte imasu
opts.en: (contradicts ならいざ知らず's setup — implies still managing it, not the expected decline)

items.why: Day 1's N ならいざ知らず — youth is set aside as a different, unknown-relevance case before stating the present limitation plainly.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼は自分の店はおろか、（ ）。
items.qr: Kare wa jibun no mise wa oroka, (___).
items.en: Not only did he lose his own shop, he even lost his home.
items.hi: उसने अपनी दुकान तो खोई ही, यहाँ तक कि घर भी खो दिया।
items.gu: તેણે પોતાની દુકાન તો ગુમાવી જ, ત્યાં સુધી કે ઘર પણ ગુમાવ્યું.

opts.t: 自宅まで失ってしまった
自宅まで自分で建てた
opts.en: (wrong — a positive achievement, but はおろか needs an escalating negative)

opts.t: 友人の店まで手伝っている
opts.r: yuujin no mise made tetsudatte iru
opts.en: (wrong — a positive/neutral action, not an escalating loss)

opts.t: 友人の店まで有名にした
opts.r: yuujin no mise made yuumei ni shita
opts.en: (wrong — a positive achievement, contradicts the negative escalation はおろか requires)

items.why: Day 1's N1はおろかN2 — losing the shop is bad, but the escalating, worse loss (his home) is what the pattern demands.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 自分の子どもを虐待するなど、（ ）。
items.qr: Jibun no kodomo o gyakutai suru nado, (___).
items.en: Abusing one's own child is conduct unbecoming of a parent.
items.hi: अपने ही बच्चे को प्रताड़ित करना, यह एक माता-पिता के तौर पर बिल्कुल अनुचित है।
items.gu: પોતાના જ બાળકને પ્રતાડિત કરવું, આ એક માતાપિતા તરીકે તદ્દન અયોગ્ય છે.

opts.t: 親にとって想像にあたらない
opts.r: oya ni totte souzou ni ataranai
opts.en: (not a valid/natural combination — 想像 pairs with 難くない, not あたらない)

opts.t: 親になれば想像に難くない
opts.r: oya ni nareba souzou ni katakunai
opts.en: (wrong tone — this would mean it's "easy to imagine," far too mild for child abuse)

opts.t: 親として失礼極まる行為だ
opts.r: oya toshite shitsurei kiwamaru koui da
opts.en: (wrong word — 失礼 means "rude," far too mild for describing abuse)

opts.t: 親としてあるまじき行為だ

items.why: Day 6's N1にあるまじきN2 — child abuse is fundamentally incompatible with the role of a parent.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: このような不当な判決には、怒りを禁じ得ません。（ ）。
items.qr: Kono you na futou na hanketsu ni wa, ikari o kinjiemasen. (___).
items.en: I cannot suppress my anger at such an unjust verdict. I intend to protest firmly.
items.hi: इस तरह के अन्यायपूर्ण फ़ैसले पर ग़ुस्सा रोक नहीं पा रहा/रही। मैं दृढ़ता से विरोध करने का इरादा रखता/रखती हूँ।
items.gu: આવા અન્યાયી ચુકાદા પર ગુસ્સો રોકી શકતો/શકતી નથી. હું દૃઢતાથી વિરોધ કરવાનો ઇરાદો ધરાવું છું.

opts.t: 理由によっては、受け入れたいです
opts.r: riyuu ni yotte wa, ukeiretai desu

opts.t: まったく受け入れられなくはありません
opts.en: (contradicts the stated anger — implies acceptance is possible)

opts.t: 断固、抗議するつもりです
やはり、抗議せずにすむでしょう
opts.r: yahari, kougi sezu ni sumu deshou
opts.en: (contradicts the uncontrollable anger — implies no protest is needed)

items.why: Day 4's N を禁じ得ない — uncontrollable anger at an unjust verdict naturally leads to a determined protest, not acceptance.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: しかし、（ ）私も弟も、男の人がほんとうに怒ったときの怖さを知らぬまま大人になってしまった。

opts.t: よいにつきわるいにつき
opts.r: yoi ni tsuki warui ni tsuki
opts.en: (not a valid/natural form — につき means "due to/per," not this idiom's につけ)

items.why: Day 6's 良かれ悪しかれ — growing up fatherless shaped the siblings for better or worse, without specifying which.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: （ ）、私たちを育てる過程で、人からうしろ指をさされるようなことだけはない子どもたちに育てなければという気負いが母にはあったと思う。

opts.en: (wrong — this signals an escalating contrast, not a causal continuation)
(wrong — a listing conjunction "as well as," not a causal link)
(wrong — also a listing conjunction, not causal)

items.why: The mother's strong pride in not being lumped with divorced single mothers (previous paragraph) is the reason for her determination in raising the children — a causal link that それゆえに supplies.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 私も弟もグレこそしなかったが、節目節目には多かれ少なかれ人並みに（ ）。

opts.t: 反抗期というものを迎えた
opts.r: hankouki to iu mono o mukaeta
opts.en: went through what's called a rebellious phase

opts.t: 迎えた反抗期に気付かなかった
opts.en: (wrong — contradicts the mother's clearly noticing and reacting to it)

opts.t: 母に反抗できずにすんだ
opts.r: haha ni hankou dekizu ni sunda
opts.en: (wrong — contradicts the mother's own exasperated reaction, which implies they DID rebel)

opts.t: 母の反抗をものともしなかった
opts.r: haha no hankou o mono to mo shinakatta
opts.en: (wrong — reverses who is rebelling against whom)

items.why: The mother's despondent quote right after ("a mother alone isn't enough... we need a father to give a good hard knock") only makes sense if the children went through a normal rebellious phase she felt unequipped to handle alone.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: そうは言っても、女親としては母はかなり厳しいほうだったと私は思っている。（ ）母は、本気で私たちを叱るときは容赦なく平手でパチンとやった。

opts.en: (wrong — needs a second, more extreme escalation noun, not this standalone use)

opts.t: 小さいことじゃあるまいし
opts.en: (wrong — dismisses "small matters" as untrue, contradicting the sentence's own point that even small matters counted)

opts.t: どんな小さいことにつき
opts.en: (wrong — につき means "regarding/due to," not "no matter how small")

opts.t: どんな小さなことであれ
opts.en: no matter how small the matter

items.why: Day 1's どんな〜であれ — however minor the issue, the mother's strict scolding applied unconditionally.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 「テレビのほうばっかり、よそ見しているからでしょ！」とゴツンとやられ、（ ）パチッとテレビを消された。

opts.en: (wrong — means "or," presenting alternatives, but both things happened together)
(wrong — "but" implies a contrast, but turning off the TV reinforces the scolding, it doesn't contradict it)

items.why: かつ links the knock on the head and switching off the television as two things that happened together, not as alternatives or a contrast.
